patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: My back's been killing me, but now both legs feel weak and I'm numb between my legs when I sit down. And — this is embarrassing — I couldn't pee for hours, then it just dribbled out.
presentation.triageNote: 40-year-old male with low back pain followed by new weakness in both legs and numbness around the groin and inner thighs. He was unable to urinate for hours and is now leaking small amounts.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because back pain with bilateral weakness, saddle numbness, urinary retention, and overflow leakage is a time-sensitive neurologic emergency.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This patient has progressive lumbosacral neurologic deficits involving both legs, perineal sensation, and bladder function.
clinical.acuityReason: The pattern suggests compression of lower spinal nerve roots and requires rapid imaging and surgical evaluation to preserve function.
teachingPoints: Bladder symptoms and saddle numbness are critical red flags in back-pain assessment.
Delay in decompression can result in permanent motor, sensory, bladder, bowel, or sexual dysfunction.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Urgent MRI and spine consultation would likely lead to emergency decompression if nerve-root compression is confirmed.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: shifting uncomfortably, unable to settle, hand on his lower back
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a black 40-year-old man, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: shifting uncomfortably, unable to settle, one hand pressed to his lower back. Expression: uncomfortable and worried. Clearly visible: a hand on the lower back and a restless, can't-get-comfortable posture. No text, no logos.
